COLLATION RESULT: four witnesses spanning 1596-1799. All four put 山茱萸 and 龍骨 under 使. All four put 丹砂 under 畏 (or, in BCGM, in the position where 畏 belongs). None of the four knows a drug called 辰丹砂. Only BCGM has the glyph 辰.
emendations: EMENDATION, glyph 辰 → 畏. In 本草綱目（四庫全書本）卷十三 the 黄芩 string reads 「惡葱實辰丹砂牡丹藜蘆」. I read the 辰 as a corrupt or misread 畏 and would print 「惡葱實，畏丹砂、牡丹、藜蘆」. Grounds, in order of weight: (1) 神農本草經（孫星衍）1799 七情表 reads 「惡蔥實；畏丹砂、牡丹、藜蘆」 at exactly this point, i.e. the 畏 is positively attested, not conjectured; (2) 本草備要 1694 and 本草從新 1757 independently read 「畏丹皮、丹砂」, again 畏; (3) the 之才 strings in this very juan follow a fixed order 為之使 → 惡 → 畏 → 勝 → 解毒, demonstrated by the 黄連 entry on the same page reading 「…惡菊花𤣥参白鮮皮芫花白殭蠶畏款冬牛膝勝烏頭解巴豆毒」, and 辰 sits in the 畏 slot, between the last 惡 item and the first 畏 item; (4) no source in the corpus records a materia medica item named 辰丹砂 in a 七情 list. I flag rather than silently normalise: I have not seen the Siku manuscript plate, only the Wikisource transcription, so the physical cause (illegible original, transcriber error, or an intruded gloss) is not established.

ALTERNATIVE HYPOTHESIS for the same glyph, recorded so it is not lost. 辰砂 is a genuine and common alternate name for cinnabar (Chen-prefecture cinnabar, = 丹砂). So 辰 could instead be an intruded marginal gloss or dittograph on 丹砂 rather than a corrupted 畏. This does NOT change the customer-facing fix: under either hypothesis 辰 is not part of a drug name and must not be displayed as one, and the 畏 relation for 丹砂/牡丹/藜蘆 is independently attested by Sun Xingyan 1799 and does not depend on this emendation. It is precisely because 辰砂 is a real drug name that the current data is dangerous: 「辰丹砂」 reads to a customer as a plausible substance.

NOT an emendation, orthographic variants only, recorded so nobody 'fixes' them later. The Siku transcription writes 黄 (U+9EC4) where Sun writes 黃 (U+9EC3); 葱 where Sun writes 蔥; 𤣥 for 玄; 参 for 參; 黄茋 for 黃芪; 䑕瘻 for 鼠瘻. Same words throughout.

SCOPE VARIANT, not an emendation. 本草綱目 1596 and 孫星衍 1799 name the whole drug 牡丹; 本草備要 1694 and 本草從新 1757 name the part 丹皮 (= 牡丹皮, root bark). I would file the 畏 relation against 牡丹 per the two primary witnesses and carry 丹皮 as a variant reading, rather than pick one silently.

CORRECTED SPLIT for H142 黃芩, one line:

(a) 辰 is not part of a drug name. Under the reading I recommend it is the 畏 of the Siku transcription. The live bug is that a paying customer currently sees 「辰丹砂」 rendered as a substance; since 辰砂 IS a real synonym for cinnabar, this misreading is credible rather than obviously garbled, which is what makes it worth fixing rather than tolerating.

THIRD DEFECT FOUND, not in the brief, flagged not fixed. The stored string 之才曰「惡葱實辰丹砂牡丹藜蘆」 has dropped the 使 clause entirely. The BCGM sentence opens 「之才曰山茱萸龍骨為之使」 before the 惡 list. So the database is currently missing both positive envoy relations. I have supplied them as positive_pairings entries above. Whoever applies this should check whether the ingest script for this herb truncates at the first negative verb, because if it does, the same two-relation loss will be present in every 之才 string that opens with 為之使 — which is most of them. 黃連 on the same page is an immediate candidate to spot-check (「黄芩龍骨理石為之使…」).

ALSO PRESENT and NOT captured, positive 得-pairings from the same 之才 sentence and from 時珍 immediately after. These are compatibility statements and must never render as warnings. Verbatim from 本草綱目 卷十三: 「得厚朴黄連止腹痛　得五味子牡蠣令人有子　得黄茋白歛赤小豆療䑕瘻　時珍曰得酒上行　得豬膽汁除肝膽火　得柴胡退寒熱　得芍藥治下痢　得桑白皮瀉肺火　得白术安胎」. I did not file these as correctedEntries because they are outside the named defect, but they are attested and free to add, with the first three attributed to 之才 and the rest to 時珍.

RELATION-DIRECTION WARNING for whoever loads this. 七情 relations in these tables are directional and are NOT automatically reciprocal. 黃芩 is listed as an envoy FOR 黃連 (「黃連　黃芩、龍骨、理石為使」) and FOR 大黃 (「大黃　黃芩為使」) and FOR 冬葵子 (「冬葵子　黃芩為使」); 黃芩 is what OTHER drugs fear or are antagonised by in 款冬花 (「畏…黃芩」), 干薑 (「惡…黃芩」), 鉤吻 (「惡黃芩」), 蜂子 (「畏黃芩」) and 露蜂房 (「惡…黃芩」). None of those belong on the Huang Qin record as Huang Qin's own 畏/惡 — they are the other drug's entry. If the ingest builds a symmetric graph, this herb will accumulate false warnings from all five.

NO CLINICAL CONTRAINDICATION was touched. The 附方 formulas in this entry were not read for scope because nothing in this defect attaches to one. The Qing handbooks do carry a herb-level caution (本草從新: 「過服損胃…血虚、寒中者禁用」 / 本草備要 same) but that is a separate field and a separate defect; I did not file it.

emendations: 卷13 苦參 氣味, character 2 of the 時珍 clause. The Wikisource Siku Quanshu transcription reads 水 (water); I read it as 汞 (mercury) and emend accordingly. Grounds: (a) two independent witnesses of the Jinling/standard lineage read 汞 (punctuated Wikisource 本草綱目/草之二 and ctext.org 本草綱目 草之二, both 「時珍曰：伏汞，製雌黃、焰硝。」); (b) the two companion objects 雌黃 and 焰硝 are minerals, so a third object 'water' breaks the series; (c) 伏汞 is a standard alchemical idiom and recurs across BCGM, e.g. 卷13 杜衡 「取自然汁可伏硫砒制汞」 and 卷13 水仙 「土宿真君曰：取汁伏汞，煮雄黃，拒火」; (d) graphically 汞 is 工 over 水, so loss of the 工 element yields exactly 水; (e) the Siku Wikisource page itself carries an uncollated banner: 「請根據四庫全書掃描版校對本頁」, i.e. it has not been checked against the Siku scan, so its authority at this point is low. NOT flagged as certain from the Siku scan itself, which I could not view; the emendation rests on the two Jinling-lineage witnesses plus the internal evidence.

熖消 in the Siku transcription = 焰硝 in the punctuated recension. Orthographic variants of the same drug (niter / saltpetre), not a substantive difference. Recommend storing 焰硝 with 熖消 noted as the Siku graph.
制 vs 製: the Siku transcription uses 制, the punctuated recensions use 製. Same word, interchangeable graphs. No substantive difference.
The Siku transcription writes the headword variously as 苦參 and 苦参 within the same volume. Cosmetic.
fixes.notes:
WHAT TO FIX, in one line: the character is 汞 (mercury), not 水 (water). Both the H214 record and the upstream harvest string must be changed from 伏水制雌黄熖消 to 伏汞，製雌黃、焰硝, and the gloss changed from \"subdues water\" to \"subdues mercury; controls orpiment and niter\".

SECOND, EQUALLY IMPORTANT FIX: the relation polarity. 伏 and 制 are POSITIVE relations. Ku Shen is the agent that controls those three minerals, they are not things Ku Shen conflicts with. This clause belongs in positive_pairings and must never surface to a customer as an incompatibility, a contraindication, or an avoidance. Please check which field the current H214 record has it in.

WHY THE TWO READINGS EXIST, so the harvest can be fixed at source rather than patched: the corruption is a recension artefact, not a random typo. The Wikisource Siku Quanshu (四庫全書) transcription of BCGM 卷13 genuinely carries 伏水 at this point. Any harvester pointed at the Siku subpages will keep re-importing 水. The Jinling-lineage text, which is what every modern printed BCGM and every scholarly citation follows, reads 伏汞. If the harvest source is the Siku series, either switch this field to the punctuated 本草綱目/草之N series or add a collation pass, otherwise the defect returns on the next harvest.

fixes.notes:
DEFECT STATUS: resolved. 「畏萆。」 is 畏萆薢 (Dioscorea hypoglauca). 本草綱目 卷十三 gives it in full and uncorrupted — 「之才曰：……畏萆薢，殺附子毒，惡藜蘆、白歛、乾薑、芫花。」 — so the substance identification rests on a clean witness, not on a reconstruction.

ON THE PROVENANCE OF THE TRUNCATION — this is where I want to be precise, because the task framing offered "the 1757 printing genuinely truncates it" as a live possibility, and it is not. The truncation is in the DIGITAL TEXT, at the level of the character 薢, and it is systematic. The same Wikisource 本草從新 file heads the Bi Xie monograph itself (卷五) as bare 「萆」, drops 薢 in three other unrelated entries, and drops 耆/芪 after 黃 four times. The 本草備要 file preserves the loss as a literal blank space: 「畏萆 。」. A printing does not abbreviate a drug's own monograph title. So: record it as a transcription truncation with the full name restored, exactly as instructed. Do not annotate the DB with a claim that Wu Yiluo abbreviated the name.

WHAT I COULD NOT DO: I did not see a scan or facsimile of the 1757 woodblock 本草從新, nor of the 1694 本草備要. ctext.org is CAPTCHA-gated and returned nothing, and Wikisource carries only 本草從新/凡例, /原序, /卷十八 and /藥性總義 as separate subpages — the 防風 text lives in the single main-page dump, whose underlying edition is not stated in its header. So the claim "the 1757 printing reads 畏萆薢 in full" is INFERRED (very strongly, from the systematic-glyph-loss evidence plus the 本草綱目 witness), not VERIFIED against a scan. The claim "the digital transcription reads bare 萆" is VERIFIED. If the DB records a per-witness verbatim string for 從新, either restore it as 畏萆薢 with an editorial flag, or hold the 從新 citation and cite 本草綱目 卷十三 instead — which is the safer option and the one I recommend.

ON 殺附子毒 — POSITIVE, confirmed by three independent witnesses with identical wording, and it must be filed as positive. 本草綱目 卷十三 and 本草從新/本草備要 all place it in the same clause block as the 畏/惡 warnings, which is very likely how it got mis-parsed into a warning field in the first place: the negative and positive relations sit in one undelimited run of text (「畏萆薢殺附子毒惡藜蘆白歛乾薑芫花」). Any parser splitting that run on drug names rather than on relation verbs will produce both a spurious 「畏附子」 and a lost positive. Worth checking whether other herbs in the DB carry the same parse failure — 黃連 in the same 諸藥制使 table has the identical shape (「畏款冬；勝烏頭；解巴豆毒」).

SECOND POSITIVE AT RISK ON THIS HERB: 「防風能制黄茋，黄茋得防風其功愈大，乃相畏而相使者也」 (杲曰, i.e. Li Dongyuan). The phrase 相畏 sits inside a clause whose whole point is that the pairing is beneficial — it is the doctrinal basis of 玉屏風散, where Fang Feng and Huang Qi are used together deliberately. If the DB currently carries 「畏黃耆」 for this herb, that is a false warning against the single most common classical Fang Feng pairing, and it is a customer-facing error of the same class as the one you asked me to fix. I have filed it under positive_pairings with relation 制; flagging it explicitly because it was not in the task brief.

SEPARATE DISCREPANCY, not the assigned defect: the 惡 list differs by witness. 本草綱目 and 神農本草經(孫) both give four drugs including 藜蘆; 本草從新 and 本草備要 give only three and omit 藜蘆. Per the working agreement I am not picking between them — surfacing both. If the DB's 惡 row was sourced from 從新 it is short one drug, and 藜蘆 is not a trivial omission.

emendations: BCGM 卷18上 line 130 prints 枸杞 with a rare-glyph placeholder: the raw wikitext reads 「枸{{SKchar2|230}}為之使」. I read {{SKchar2|230}} as 杞, on two grounds: the compound 枸_ in an envoy clause, and the explicit 「枸杞為使」 / 「枸杞为使」 in the 1799 七情表, 本草備要 1694 and 本草從新 1757. Flagged, not silently normalised.

BCGM 卷18上 renders 栝 inside 栝蔞 with placeholder {{SKchar|2201}} throughout the 附方 (e.g. 「{{SKchar|2201}}蔞仁一兩」), and once as the digraph {{SKchar|607}}{{SKchar|624}} (Li Shizhen's 釋名 notes the graphic variant: 「亦作𠣤𧅄，後人又轉為栝蔞」). Read all as 栝蔞. The headword itself at line 121 is written in full: 栝樓.

干薑 (1799 七情表) vs 乾薑 (BCGM 1596, 從新 1757) vs 干姜 (備要, simplified copy). One drug, Zingiberis Rhizoma, dried ginger. 干 is the orthographic variant of 乾, NOT the separate drug 干 or a scribal error. Do not split into two entries.

白芨 in the aconite row of the 1799 text is the standard 十八反 drug 白及 (Bletilla). Variant graph. Immaterial here since the whole token is being removed from H283, but recorded so the correction is not mistaken for a substitution.

The Wikisource 本草從新 transcription is mixed simplified/traditional (乌頭, 栝蒌, 虚, 郁, 荡, 脓). I have given traditional readings in the evidence block (烏頭, 栝蔞, 虛). The 本草備要 Wikisource copy is fully simplified throughout; its lines are quoted as found and then transliterated, never presented as the traditional original.
The 1799 appendix spells this herb 栝蔞 in its own row (line 3639) but 栝樓 in the 蜀漆 row (line 3711). Same drug; 蔞/樓 is the variant Li Shizhen discusses at BCGM 卷18上 釋名 (「愈轉愈失其眞矣」). Not two herbs.

Headword scope differs across witnesses and should be understood as whole-drug: the 本經 drug proper is the ROOT (孫本 headword 栝蔞根), BCGM attaches Xu Zhicai's 七情 to the 根/天花粉 subsection, while 本草備要 and 本草從新 attach the identical set to the SEED (栝樓仁) and then say the root is 「畏惡同」. No witness restricts the set to one part, so 使/惡/畏/反 apply to Trichosanthes as a drug. The two clinical contraindications, by contrast, ARE part-scoped and are recorded as such.

SNBCJ line 1538 (the 案 philological note under 栝蔞根) contains several illegible/blanked glyphs in the transcription, e.g. 「《說文》云：　，　蔞，果也」. That passage is etymological only and carries no relation data, so nothing in this correction depends on it. Noted so the gap is on record.
fixes.notes:
WHAT THE DEFECT ACTUALLY WAS, and what the corrected row looks like.

(a) The composite row. 「栝蔞　枸杞為使；惡干薑；畏牛膝、乾漆；反烏頭。」 is not a 反 statement. It is the whole 七情 line for the drug, semicolon-delimited, carrying four different verbs. Filing it whole under 反 did two separate kinds of damage: it flattened three grades of severity into the corpus's most serious one, and it dragged 枸杞為使 into an incompatibility field. 使 / 為之使 is the ENVOY relation, a guiding partner drug. Goji is a recommended co-prescription for Trichosanthes, so the pre-correction record was telling paying customers the exact opposite of what the source says. That is the highest-consequence error on this row after the aconite question, because it is inverted rather than merely misgraded, and a practitioner acting on it would drop a partner drug the classical text recommends.

Correctly split, this herb's own relations are:
  使 (envoy, POSITIVE): 枸杞 goji
  惡 (antagonised by): 乾薑 dried ginger
  畏 (diminished by): 牛膝 Achyranthes, and 乾漆 dried lacquer, as TWO items
  反 (opposes, 十八反): 烏頭 aconite
Five relations, four verbs, one row.

(b) The aconite import. 「烏頭、烏喙　莽草為使，反半夏、栝蔞、貝母、白蘞、白芨」 is ACONITE'S row, read from the wrong side. It is the familiar 十八反 verse 「半蔞貝蘞及攻烏」 in prose form: the five drugs that oppose aconite. Only the 栝蔞 token concerns this herb.

STATED PLAINLY, as asked: the aconite entry is CORROBORATION of 反烏頭 and is NOT a source of any further pairings for H283. Its evidential value is exactly one bit, that the 反 between Trichosanthes and aconite is attested reciprocally from both sides of the pair. It contributes no new incompatibility. Everything else on that line belongs to aconite:
  莽草為使 is aconite's OWN envoy, and it is positive besides. Nothing to do with Trichosanthes on either count.
  半夏、貝母、白蘞、白芨 are aconite's four other antagonists. Carried into this herb's list they fabricate four warnings that no source supports.

The 半夏 item is worth calling out specifically, because it is falsifiable from within the same corpus rather than merely unsupported. Bencao Gangmu 卷18上 appends three formulas that combine Trichosanthes WITH ban xia, including Zhang Zhongjing's own 「加半夏四兩更善」 (Jingui Yaolue, i.e. 栝樓薤白半夏湯). The pre-correction record therefore warned against a pairing that its own principal source prescribes.

反烏頭 SURVIVES, CONFIRMED. This was the item most at risk from the cleanup, since the corrupt aconite row was the more conspicuous of the two carriers and deleting it could have taken the real relation with it. It does not depend on that row. It is independently attested in this herb's own entry in all four witnesses I read: 1799 七情表 (「反烏頭」), BCGM 1596 之才曰 (「反烏頭」), 本草備要 1694 (「反乌头」), 本草從新 1757 (「反烏頭」). It is a 十八反 relation, the most serious grade in the corpus, and it must retain maximum warning severity and cover the whole aconite group (烏頭 / 烏喙 / 附子 / 天雄 / 川烏 / 草烏), the reciprocal being confirmed at 本草備要 附子: 「反贝母、半夏、栝蒌、白芨、白蔹。」

NET SAFETY EFFECT of the correction: one false warning removed by promotion to positive (枸杞), five false warnings removed as another drug's data (莽草 plus the four aconite antagonists), one genuine 惡 and two genuine 畏 recovered at their correct severity rather than inflated to 反, and the one genuine 反 preserved intact.

TWO RECIPROCAL ENTRIES, handled deliberately rather than dropped. 「蜀漆　栝樓為使」 and 「秦椒　惡栝蔞、防葵」 both name this herb but are headed under other drugs. I have recorded them with the direction stated explicitly in the gloss and the reversal marked in the scope field. Neither belongs in this herb's own 使/惡/畏/反 set, and 防葵 in particular is Qin Jiao's second object and has no relation to Trichosanthes. If the schema cannot carry directionality on a pairing, these two should be dropped rather than flattened, since a direction-blind render of 「秦椒　惡栝蔞」 recreates exactly the class of error being fixed here.

SCOPE NOTE ON THE CLINICAL ENTRIES. The two clinical contraindications I added are part-scoped and are marked as such: 「寒胃滑腸。胃虚食少。脾虚泄瀉。勿投。」 attaches to the seed (栝蔞仁) and 「脾胃虚寒者。均宜戒用。」 to the root (天花粉). The 七情 relations, by contrast, are whole-drug: no witness restricts them to a part, and where 備要 and 從新 site them on the seed they immediately add 「畏惡同」 for the root. Do not let the part-scoping of the clinical lines propagate to the relation rows, or vice versa.

NOT VERIFIED, and therefore not asserted. I did not check what the live H283 record currently contains; I worked from the defect description plus the sources. Whoever applies this should confirm the two defective rows are the only carriers of the imported aconite tokens before deleting, since 半夏, 貝母, 白蘞 and 白芨 may also have been written into the herb's incompatibility list as free-standing rows during an earlier normalisation pass, in which case those too are spurious and need removing.

correctedEntries.text: 斆曰凡使天麻勿用御風草二物相似只是葉莖不同御風草根莖斑葉背白有青㸃使御風草即勿使天麻若同用令人有腸結之患
correctedEntries.speaker: 斆 = 雷斆 (Lei Xiao), Liu-Song dynasty, author of 雷公炮炙論. Speaker identified from BCGM 卷01上 序例: 「時珍曰劉宋時雷斆所著非黄帝時雷公也」. 欽定古今圖書集成 草木典 卷156 quotes the same clause as 《雷斆》曰.
correctedEntries.scope: whole drug (天麻, the root). Not formula-scoped: 凡使天麻 = whenever Tian Ma is used at all. Not scoped to 赤箭 (the aerial stem drug) or 還筒子 (the seed), which have their own 主治 in the same entry. The prohibition is reciprocal, stated in both directions (勿用御風草 / 使御風草即勿使天麻), and 雷公炮炙論 repeats it verbatim under its own 御風草 entry.
correctedEntries.gloss: Lei Xiao: whenever you use Tian Ma, do not use 御風草 with it. The two are alike, differing only in leaf and stem: 御風草 has a mottled root and stem, and the leaf underside is white with green dots. If you are using 御風草, then do not use Tian Ma. Used together they cause 腸結, intestinal blockage, in the patient. This is a bilateral co-use prohibition between two named drugs with a named adverse outcome, and must render as a warning.

correctedEntries.text: 斆曰修事天麻十両剉安于瓶中用蒺藜子一鎰緩火熬焦盖于天麻上以三重紙封繫從巳至未取出蒺藜炒過葢繫如前凡七遍用布拭上氣汗刀劈焙乾單搗用若用御風草亦同此法
correctedEntries.speaker: 斆 = 雷斆 (Lei Xiao), 雷公炮炙論, quoted in BCGM 修治 section
correctedEntries.scope: whole drug (天麻 root), 修治 / processing section only
correctedEntries.gloss: Lei Xiao's processing method: 10 liang of Tian Ma, cut up, placed in a jar under 1 yi of Tribulus (蒺藜子) roasted dark over a slow fire, sealed with three layers of paper from the si to the wei double-hour, the Tribulus re-fried and re-covered, seven times through; then wiped of surface moisture, split with a knife, dried over gentle heat, and pounded alone. Closing line: if you are using 御風草, the same method applies. Included here only because it names 御風草 and must NOT be harvested as a second incompatibility clause. It is a processing instruction, not a warning.

emendations: SPEAKER GLYPH DROPPED IN ONE RECENSION. In the punctuated Wikisource recension 本草綱目/草之一, the speaker name is missing at this exact clause: the text reads a literal ASCII space (0x20) where 斆 should stand, giving 「…如人參中之神參也。 曰︰凡使天麻…」. Byte check: e59ba3 e4b99f e38082 20 e69bb0. Reading I would use: 斆曰. Grounds: the Siku recension 卷12下 reads 斆曰 intact, and 古今圖書集成 卷156 reads 《雷斆》曰 in full. Anyone harvesting from the punctuated recension alone will get an unattributed clause and may drop it as speakerless. Flagging, not silently normalising.

VARIANT GLYPH 㸃 (U+3E03). The Siku recension writes 葉背白有青㸃. 㸃 is a variant orthography of 點. Reading I would use: 點. Both the punctuated BCGM recension and 古今圖書集成 read 青點. This is a graphic variant only, no change of sense.

TEXTUAL VARIANT 葉背白 vs 叶皆白. Three witnesses (Siku BCGM 卷12下, punctuated BCGM 草之一, 古今圖書集成 卷156) all read 葉背白, leaf underside white. The Wikisource 雷公炮炙論 digitization reads 叶皆白, leaves entirely white. Reading I would use: 葉背白. Grounds: 葉背 (abaxial leaf surface) is a standard discriminator in this literature and is the majority reading; the 雷公炮炙論 page is tagged 未校訂 (unproofread), is a simplified-character transcription of a lost text known only through quotation, and carries visible OCR corruption in the adjacent lines (the string 'KT ' stands in for an unrecovered graph in 緩火KT 焦熟後, where BCGM's parallel reads 緩火熬焦). Weakest witness of the four.

fixes.notes:
VERDICT ON THE DEFECT: confirmed, and the auditor is right that it is the most safety-load-bearing item on the row. It belongs in drug_incompatibilities. It must not sit in unclassified, and it must render as a warning.

WHY IT IS NOT A 七情 RELATION, AND WHY I LEFT `relation` EMPTY
I checked the 52-character clause against every 七情 verb. None is present. The operative verbs are 勿用 (do not use), 勿使 (do not employ) and 同用 (use together). There is no 畏, no 惡, and critically no 反. So this is a co-use prohibition of a different kind from the 七情: it is a Lei Gong 炮炙 (processing-tradition) prohibition, transmitted in the 修治/辨疑 register rather than the 七情 register. Functionally it does the same work as a 相反 pairing, and clinically it is at least as serious, since it names a specific harm. But labelling it 反 would put words in Lei Xiao's mouth and would falsely enrol it in the 十八反, which it is not part of. Hence: correct field, empty relation verb, with the categorical basis recorded in the gloss.

THE MISCLASSIFICATION TRAP, WHICH IS PROBABLY WHAT BROKE THIS ROW
The clause contains 使 three times: 凡使天麻, 使御風草, 勿使天麻. In all three it is the ordinary verb "to use/employ" (the standard Lei Gong opener 凡使X = "whenever using X"). It is NOT the 七情 使 of 為之使 / 相使, "envoy". Any matcher keying on the bare character 使 will either (a) misread this as a POSITIVE envoy pairing and render 御風草 as a recommended partner, which would invert a safety warning into a recommendation, or (b) detect the conflict, fail to resolve it, and dump the clause into unclassified. Outcome (b) is what appears to have happened, and it is the better of the two failures. Recommend the matcher require 為之使 / 相使 / 為使 as the trigger for the positive 使 relation, and treat bare 使 preceded by 凡 or 勿 as the plain verb. The same fix protects every other Lei Xiao 凡使 line in the corpus, which is most of the 修治 sections.

SCOPE: WHOLE DRUG, NOT FORMULA-SCOPED
No 附方 attachment. The clause sits at the tail of 集解 (the identification and description section), and the wording 凡使天麻 is maximally general. The two 附方 in this entry (天麻丸 and the 腰脚疼痛 compress of 天麻半夏細辛) are downstream and unrelated. The prohibition is also reciprocal, and 雷公炮炙論 states it a second time under its own 御風草 entry, which confirms drug-level rather than preparation-level scope.

WHAT 御風草 IS, PER THE SOURCE
BCGM does not identify it botanically, and I am not going to guess. What the source actually gives:
1. It is a real, distinct drug in the Lei Gong tradition, not merely an adulterant name. 雷公炮炙論 gives it its own entry in 中卷 with its own 修治 method, identical to Tian Ma's Tribulus-jar method. BCGM compresses this to 「若用御風草亦同此法」.
2. Lei Xiao's discriminators, and these are the only description anywhere: root and stem mottled/spotted (根莖斑), leaf underside white with green dots (葉背白有青㸃). The confusion risk is explicitly stated: 二物相似, only leaf and stem differ.
3. The name means "ward off wind", and 天麻 itself carries the alias 定風草 "settle-the-wind herb" (BCGM 卷12下 釋名, citing 藥性論). The two names are near-synonymous in sense, which is very likely part of why they were confused in the trade. That is my inference from the source, flagged as inference, not a source statement.
4. Searched Wikisource full-text for 御風草 across the whole corpus: it occurs only in BCGM (both recensions), in 古今圖書集成 quoting BCGM, and in 雷公炮炙論. It occurs 0 times in the Sun Xingyan 神農本草經, 0 times in 本草從新, 0 times in 本草備要, and 0 times in the 證類本草 juan I hold. No source in reach identifies it with a named species. Status: UNKNOWN, and it should be shipped as unknown with Lei Xiao's morphology attached, never with a guessed binomial.

A SECOND, DIFFERENT LOOK-ALIKE ON THIS ROW, WHICH I DID NOT TOUCH
Do not confuse the 御風草 problem with the 天麻草 problem. The 【正誤】 section of the same entry records that 陳藏器 described a different plant under the name 天麻 (「生平澤，似馬鞭草，節節生紫花」), which 陳承 and 李時珍 reject as unrelated: 「陳氏所說，乃一種天麻草，是益母草之類是也」, wrongly imported into the Tian Ma entry by 嘉祐本草. That is a genuine not_this_herb item, but it is a separate item from this defect and I have not written an entry for it, per the surgical-edit rule. Flagging it only so a future pass does not merge the two look-alikes into one row. The 御風草 clause is a SAFETY item; the 天麻草 clause is a NOMENCLATURE item.

ON SPLITTING THE CLAUSE
The middle sub-clause (二物相似只是葉莖不同御風草根莖斑葉背白有青㸃) is, on its own, not_this_herb material: it is a look-alike discrimination. I deliberately did NOT split it out. Splitting would either duplicate text across two fields or, worse, separate the morphological warning from the harm statement 令人有腸結之患 that gives it its force. Recommend keeping the clause whole in drug_incompatibilities and, if the not_this_herb field needs the discriminator, cross-referencing rather than copying.

METHOD NOTE
All sources fetched with curl and grepped locally per the brief. WebFetch was not used. ctext.org was not needed. Every citation above was read from a file on disk in this session; the primary 卷12下 download was re-fetched fresh (HTTP 200, 78,231 bytes) and byte-compared identical to a prior copy before I relied on it.

correctedEntries.speaker: 雷斆 (Lei Xiao), quoted in BCGM as 「斆曰」; the underlying source is the 雷公炮炙論, cited in 證類本草 as 「雷公云」
correctedEntries.scope: named part — the ROOT only. The clause sits inside the section headed 「根修治」 (root, preparation) in the 茜草 entry. BCGM treats 根 and 苗根 as separate drugs in the same entry (「别錄曰苗根鹹平無毒」), so this attaches to 茜根, not to the aerial parts and not to any 附方.
correctedEntries.gloss: Do not use 赤柳草根 (red-willow root); it looks genuinely identical [to qiancao root], it is only sour and astringent in taste. Taking it by mistake causes 内障眼 (internal obstruction of the eye / cataract). Drink licorice water at once to stop it, and the toxic qi disperses. Punctuated exactly this way in the 1726 古今圖書集成 witness: 「勿用赤柳草根，真相似，只是味酸濇，誤服令人患內障眼。速服甘草水止之，即毒氣散。」 This is a real safety item, not preparation doctrine: it is a stated 勿用 (do not use) against a named adulterant, with a named harm and a named antidote. It is an ADULTERANT warning, i.e. the harm comes from the substitute plant, not from Rubia cordifolia itself, and must be rendered so that it never reads as a toxicity of qiancao.

correctedEntries.text: 凡使用銅刀於槐砧上剉日乾勿犯鉛鐵氣
correctedEntries.speaker: 雷斆 (Lei Xiao), quoted in BCGM as 「斆曰」; 雷公炮炙論 via 證類本草
correctedEntries.scope: named part — the ROOT. Same 「根修治」 section, immediately preceding the adulterant clause in the BCGM ordering.
correctedEntries.gloss: Whenever using it, chop it with a COPPER knife on a block of Chinese-scholartree (槐) wood, and sun-dry it. Do not let it come into contact with the qi of lead or iron. This is processing doctrine (which tools and which drying), NOT a safety warning and NOT a 七情 relation. The 證類本草 recension words the same rule as 「勿犯鐡并鈆」 (do not let it contact iron and lead) and places it AFTER the adulterant clause rather than before it.

correctedEntries.speaker: 汪昂 Wang Ang, 本草備要 (1694), 草部 茜草
correctedEntries.scope: named part — the ROOT (「根可染絳」).
correctedEntries.gloss: The root can dye crimson; avoid iron. This is the later, compressed form of the same Lei Xiao processing rule, and confirms that 忌鐵 in the circulating literature is a restatement of 勿犯鉛鐵氣 — preparation doctrine, not a contraindication. EMENDATION FLAG: the only reachable transcription of 本草備要 is in SIMPLIFIED characters, reading 「根可染绛，忌铁。」 The traditional reading given here is my restoration, not the transcription as found.

correctedEntries.speaker: 徐之才 Xu Zhicai, 藥對, quoted in BCGM 氣味 as 「之才曰」 and in BCGM 卷二 序例下
correctedEntries.gloss: Fears / is diminished by 鼠姑. NEGATIVE — this is a genuine 七情 warning relation. Independently attested in three places: BCGM 卷十八下 氣味 (1596), BCGM 卷二 序例下 相須相使相畏相惡諸藥 (1596), and the 諸藥制使 appendix of the Sun Xingyan 神農本草經 (1799), which reads 「茜根　畏鼠姑。」 The 證類本草 (1082) head-note writes it 「畏䑕姑」, 䑕 being the older graph for 鼠. Identity caution: 鼠姑 is used in the corpus both as an alias of 牡丹 (Paeonia suffruticosa root bark — the SBCJ 牡丹 entry itself states 「一名鹿韭，一名鼠姑」) and as a name for a woodlouse-type insect drug; the sources do not disambiguate here, so the target should NOT be silently resolved to 牡丹 in the database.

correctedEntries.speaker: 徐之才 Xu Zhicai, 藥對, quoted in BCGM 氣味 as 「之才曰」
correctedEntries.scope: whole drug — specifically the expressed juice (汁) of qiancao acting ON realgar
correctedEntries.gloss: Its juice controls / subdues 雄黄 (realgar, arsenic disulphide). POSITIVE — 制 means qiancao juice curbs the toxicity of realgar, i.e. qiancao is the controlling agent. This must NEVER render as a warning or as an incompatibility. It appears in BCGM 卷十八下 as 「畏鼠姑汁制雄黄」, an unpunctuated run that must be parsed 「畏鼠姑，汁制雄黄」 (two separate relations); BCGM 卷二 序例下 lists the same drug as 「茜根　畏鼠姑制雄黄」, confirming the split. A parser that reads this as one clause would wrongly produce '畏 鼠姑汁' or attach 雄黄 to 畏.

correctedEntries.speaker: 汪昂 Wang Ang, 本草備要 (1694), 草部 茜草
correctedEntries.gloss: Those with deficient blood should avoid using it. This is a genuine clinical contraindication and is distinct from the adulterant warning above. DEFECT STATUS: RESOLVED. The adulterant-toxicity warning quoted in the task exists in the BCGM 茜草 entry essentially word for word and is confirmed against three independent recensions plus its pre-BCGM source. The task's quoted text matched the BCGM Siku wording character for character apart from punctuation, which the Siku transcription does not carry; the 1726 古今圖書集成 supplies punctuation identical to the task's.

WHY THE SAFETY-ITEM / PREPARATION-DOCTRINE SPLIT IS REAL AND NOT AN EDITORIAL JUDGEMENT: both clauses live in the same section, 「根修治」, and both are spoken by 雷斆. They are nevertheless different in kind, and the corpus itself separates them — 證類本草 places them in the opposite order, showing they were transmitted as two units. The metal/copper clause governs how to reduce and dry the drug you already have. The 勿用赤柳草根 clause governs which plant you have at all, and it is the only one of the two that names a harm (内障眼) and an antidote (甘草水). Anything with a named harm and a named antidote is a safety item.

CRITICAL RENDERING CONSTRAINT ON THE NEW ENTRY: the toxicity belongs to the ADULTERANT, 赤柳草根, not to Rubia cordifolia. If this ships as a bare toxicity warning on the H206 record it will tell customers that qiancao causes cataracts, which is the opposite of what the source says. The subject of 誤服 is the substitute plant. The identifying test the source gives is organoleptic, 味酸濇 (sour and astringent), offered because 真相似 — the two are visually indistinguishable.

I HAVE NOT IDENTIFIED 赤柳草根. The source names it and nothing more. Do not resolve it to a binomial in the database; a plausible identification here would be exactly the kind of invention this project has had to withdraw before. Leave it as the transliterated Chinese name with the gloss 'red willow root'.

七情 PARSE HAZARD THAT WILL BITE AN AUTOMATED IMPORTER: BCGM 卷十八下 runs two relations together unpunctuated as 「畏鼠姑汁制雄黄」. A naive split yields the nonsense relation '畏 鼠姑汁' or attaches 雄黄 to 畏, which would turn a POSITIVE relation (茜根 controls realgar's toxicity) into a warning against combining qiancao with realgar. DEFECT CONFIRMED, and the misfiling is worse than a scope error — it is a polarity inversion.

What the data has: 「咽乾乃虚中有熱不可服涼藥…」 filed as a contraindication OF astragalus.
What the source says: the sentence is the opening rationale of one 附方 in BCGM 卷12上 黃耆 — the ninth of fourteen formulas (section headed 舊五新九, five old and nine new), titled 欬[嗽]膿血, attributed to 席延賞方. The drug it forbids is 涼藥, cooling drugs, on the reasoning that a dry throat here signals heat sitting inside a deficiency (虚中有熱) rather than repletion heat, so cooling would attack the deficiency. The drug it then PRESCRIBES, in the next clause, is astragalus, 4 liang, with licorice 1 liang. A customer-facing row rendering this as "astragalus is contraindicated when the throat is dry" tells the reader the opposite of what Li Shizhen recorded.

RECOMMENDATION: strike it from clinical_contraindications outright. It is not a herb-level restriction under any reading, and it is not a restriction on this herb at all. If the project wants to preserve it, the only defensible home is a formula-scoped note on the 席延賞 huangqi-gancao powder, with the restricted substance recorded as 涼藥, not 黃耆.

fixes.notes:
DEFECT CONFIRMED, and the brief's reading of it is correct.

1. WHAT THE WHOLE RUN ACTUALLY IS. It is not a materia medica contraindication paragraph at all. It is the closing third of 吳其濬's own 案 (personal critical note) appended to the 黨參 entry in a Qing botanical treatise. His argument across leaves 93–94 is that the 黨參 of the market is NOT the ancient 上黨人參 of the classics, that the whole world substitutes it for 神草 (divine herb = true ginseng) without knowing better, and that on his own inspection the plant resembles young 苜蓿 in form and 黃耆 in taste and smell. The passage the database carries is his verdict at the end of that argument.

2. THE CORRECT BOUNDARY. Three spans, three different speech acts:
   (a) 「但太行脈厚泉甘此草味甜有汁養脾助氣亦應功亞黃耆無甚感鬱之人藉以充潤腸胃當亦小有資補」 — a CONCESSION / weak indication. Taihang's veins are deep and its springs sweet, so this plant is sweet and juicy, nourishes the spleen and assists qi, and should rank just below 黃耆; for a person with no significant 感 (external contraction) or 鬱 (stagnation), using it to fill and moisten the intestines and stomach will indeed give some small nourishment. This is who it DOES suit. Filing it as a contraindication inverts its meaning.
   (b) 「若傷冒時疫以此橫塞中焦羸尪雜症妄冀蘇起沉痾未覩其益必蒙其害」 — THE PROHIBITION. This is the only span that warns. Boundary evidence is internal and clean: 若 opens the conditional, and 必蒙其害 closes the apodosis. Everything before 若 is the concessive clause it is set against; everything after 必蒙其害 addresses the reader, not the patient.
   (c) 「世有良工其察鄙言」 — an AUTHORIAL ENVOI. "If there are skilled physicians in the world, let them examine my humble words." A closing formula of scholarly modesty. It carries no clinical content whatsoever and must not render as a warning.

3. DATE. 1848, so PRE-1900. The project's pre-1900 citation rule is satisfied. Note this is a real trap on this herb: the obvious guess for a polemical Qing-sounding 黨參 commentary is 張山雷《本草正義》, which is 1920 and would have been disqualified — but 本草正義 is emphatically pro-黨參 and is NOT the source. I verified that rather than assuming it.

4. GENRE CAVEAT WORTH CARRYING IN THE DATA. 《植物名實圖考》 is a botanical/philological work by a Qing official and plant scholar, not a physician's materia medica.
